questions.note: Answer D is best (36 h half-life, only 2 days since change), but the stem's 'well below target although dose should produce in-range' is awkwardly worded.
C best; stem says heart failure but changes are renal-clearance related; 'slowly' qualifier makes C better than A.
Standard receptor-reserve teaching: rightward shift first.
Furosemide vs thiazide: efficacy (maximal effect) is higher for loop; D correct.
G6PD hemolysis is classically idiosyncratic/genetic; a type B/pharmacogenetic framing is also used but D is best.
HIT is often classed as type II (non-IgE antibody) but not a clean Gell-Coombs fit; D is the only correct mechanism.
